fichas.title: Joinery
fichas.summary: Joinery planning covers equipment and room relationships, production flow, construction, environmental conditions, and a sample workshop layout. More compact plans are described as more economical than long sheds. Machine and bench rooms are separated by a wall with doors; the illustrated arrangement supports a sequence from timber storage and cutting through machining, assembly, finishing, storage, and dispatch.

dimensions.label: Floor area per employee
dimensions.context: Approximate space requirement for the illustrated examples, excluding open storerooms.
dimensions.ocr_raw: The space requirement for the illustrated examples is approx. 70–80 m² per employee (without open storerooms).

dimensions.label: Employees in small businesses
dimensions.context: Small-business production flow is described as linear or angled-shaped for businesses with up to approximately this number of employees.
dimensions.ocr_raw: General production flow: in small businesses with up to approx. 10 employees: linear, angled-shaped.

dimensions.label: Employees in medium-sized businesses
dimensions.context: Medium-sized businesses with over this number are described as better suited to U-shaped or circular layouts.
dimensions.ocr_raw: In medium-sized businesses with over 10 employees: U-shaped or circular (square) layouts are better for workflow.

dimensions.label: High sill height
dimensions.context: High sills for continuous strip windows.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Continuous strip windows, high sills (1.00-1.35 m).

dimensions.label: Crane load
dimensions.context: Load notation shown beside the crane in the example joinery plan.
